findings.title: OpenSSH User Enumeration via timing attack (CVE-2019-14861)
findings.description: The OpenSSH server running on port 22 (version OpenSSH 7.6p1 Ubuntu 4ubuntu0.3) is vulnerable to a user enumeration flaw (CVE-2019-14861). An attacker can determine the existence of a valid username by observing timing differences in responses to authentication attempts, even without valid credentials. This can aid in brute-force or dictionary attacks.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade OpenSSH to version 8.1 or later. Ensure that the operating system and all installed packages are kept up-to-date with security patches. Consider disabling SSH password authentication and enforcing key-based authentication only.

findings.title: Admin Panel Discovered
findings.description: An administrative interface was discovered at '/admin'. This panel could provide access to sensitive site configurations or user management features.
findings.recommendation: Ensure strong authentication mechanisms are in place, including multi-factor authentication if possible. Limit access to trusted IP addresses and enforce strict access control.

findings.title: Open Uploads Directory Found
findings.description: The '/uploads' directory is accessible and appears to be browsable. This could allow attackers to upload malicious files (e.g., webshells) or discover sensitive information if users upload private documents.
findings.recommendation: Configure the web server to prevent directory listing. Implement strict file type validation, size limits, and content sanitization for all uploads. Store uploaded files outside the web root if possible.

findings.title: Potentially Sensitive Configuration Directory
findings.description: A '/config' directory was found, which might contain sensitive configuration files (e.g., database credentials, API keys). Direct access to such files could lead to full system compromise.
findings.recommendation: Ensure that configuration files are not directly accessible via the web server. Implement appropriate file permissions and restrict access to these directories, ideally storing them outside the web root.

findings.title: Backup Directory with 403 Forbidden
findings.description: A '/backup' directory exists but returns a 403 Forbidden status. While direct access is denied, its mere existence suggests that backup files might be present and potentially discoverable through other means (e.g., misconfigured permissions on specific filenames within the directory, or directory traversal).
findings.recommendation: Verify that backup files are stored securely and are not accessible, even indirectly, from the web. Consider moving backups to an offline or restricted-access storage location and ensure no sensitive information is left in the web root.

findings.title: Missing CSP
findings.description: The Content-Security-Policy (CSP) header is not set. This allows browsers to load resources from any origin, increasing the risk of XSS and data injection attacks. Without a CSP, it's harder to mitigate the impact of cross-site scripting vulnerabilities.
findings.recommendation: Implement a robust Content-Security-Policy header to restrict the sources from which content can be loaded. Start with a strict policy and incrementally relax it as needed, ensuring it covers all legitimate scripts, styles, images, and other assets.

findings.title: Missing X-Frame-Options header
findings.description: The X-Frame-Options header is not set. This makes the website vulnerable to clickjacking attacks, where an attacker can embed the site in an iframe on their malicious page, potentially tricking users into interacting with the embedded site.
findings.recommendation: Implement the X-Frame-Options header with a value like 'DENY' or 'SAMEORIGIN' to prevent the site from being embedded in frames by other domains. 'DENY' is the most secure option.

findings.title: Missing X-XSS-Protection header
findings.description: The X-XSS-Protection header is not set. While modern browsers have robust built-in XSS filters, this header provides an additional layer of protection against reflected XSS attacks by enabling the browser's XSS auditor.
findings.recommendation: Implement the X-XSS-Protection header with a value of '1; mode=block' to enable the browser's XSS filter and instruct it to block detected attacks rather than sanitizing them.

findings.title: SQLi
findings.description: The GET parameter 'id' on the endpoint '/' (ttvideodownload.me) is vulnerable to SQL Injection. SQLMap successfully identified a time-based blind SQL injection vulnerability, allowing for arbitrary data retrieval and potentially full database compromise. The backend DBMS was identified as MySQL. This vulnerability allows an attacker to extract sensitive information from the database, bypass authentication, and in some configurations, execute operating system commands.
findings.recommendation: Implement parameterized queries or prepared statements for all database interactions to prevent SQL injection. Sanitize and validate all user inputs to ensure they conform to expected data types and formats. Avoid concatenating user-supplied input directly into SQL queries. Consider implementing a Web Application Firewall (WAF) as an additional layer of defense, but note that a WAF is not a replacement for secure coding practices. Regularly patch and update database systems and application frameworks.

findings.title: Default Credentials Found for Admin Panel
findings.description: The Metasploit `auxiliary/scanner/http/http_login` module successfully identified default credentials ('admin'/'admin') for the administrative interface located at `ttvideodownload.me/admin`. This grants full control over the website's configuration, content, and potentially user data, posing a severe risk to the application's integrity, confidentiality, and availability.
findings.recommendation: Immediately change the default administrative credentials to a strong, unique password. Implement multi-factor authentication (MFA) if available. Regularly review user accounts and permissions, ensuring no other default or weak credentials exist. Consider IP-based access restrictions for the admin panel.

findings.title: TLS 1.0 Protocol Enabled
findings.description: The server supports TLS 1.0, an outdated and insecure cryptographic protocol. This protocol is known to have several vulnerabilities and is no longer considered secure for protecting sensitive data.
findings.recommendation: Disable TLS 1.0 support on the server. Configure the server to only support TLS 1.2 or newer protocols (e.g., TLS 1.3).

findings.title: TLS 1.1 Protocol Enabled
findings.description: The server supports TLS 1.1, an outdated cryptographic protocol. While slightly better than TLS 1.0, it still lacks modern security features and is susceptible to various attacks. It is no longer recommended for secure communication.
findings.recommendation: Disable TLS 1.1 support on the server. Configure the server to only support TLS 1.2 or newer protocols (e.g., TLS 1.3).

findings.title: Weak Cipher Suites Supported
findings.description: The server supports weak cipher suites, including those with small key sizes (e.g., 64-bit, export-grade) or known cryptographic weaknesses. These ciphers can be exploited by attackers to decrypt communications.
findings.recommendation: Disable all weak and deprecated cipher suites. Prioritize strong, forward-secret cipher suites (e.g., AES256-GCM-SHA384, CHACHA20-POLY1305) and remove support for export-grade or 3DES ciphers.

findings.title: HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) Header Missing
findings.description: The HSTS header is not present. This allows man-in-the-middle attackers to downgrade connections from HTTPS to HTTP, potentially exposing users to insecure communication, even if they initially tried to access the site via HTTPS.
findings.recommendation: Implement the Strict-Transport-Security HTTP header with an appropriate max-age directive (e.g., `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload`).

findings.title: Client-Initiated Renegotiation Supported (Insecure)
findings.description: The server allows client-initiated renegotiation, which can be abused by attackers to inject plaintext into a victim's SSL session (CVE-2009-3555). While this is an old vulnerability, supporting it is a risk.
findings.recommendation: Disable client-initiated TLS renegotiation on the server. Ensure that the server only allows secure renegotiation as per RFC 5746.

findings.title: Dev Subdomain
findings.description: A development subdomain, 'dev.ttvideodownload.me', was identified. Such subdomains frequently host unpatched software, exposed internal configurations, sensitive data, or have relaxed security policies not intended for public exposure. This presents a significant attack surface that could be exploited to gain unauthorized access to internal systems or sensitive information.
findings.recommendation: Immediately review the 'dev.ttvideodownload.me' subdomain for sensitive data, exposed services, or misconfigurations. If it is not actively required, take it offline. If it must remain online, implement strict access controls (e.g., IP whitelisting, VPN access), ensure all software is fully patched and up-to-date, remove any sensitive data, and apply the same rigorous security hardening standards as production environments. Consider renaming or obscuring the subdomain to reduce its discoverability.

findings.title: CORS Wildcard
findings.description: The server responds with an 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *' header, indicating a wildcard Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) policy. This configuration allows any domain to make cross-origin requests to the application. If sensitive information or authenticated data is returned in responses, this can lead to data leakage, unauthorized access to user data, or other security bypasses from malicious third-party websites, especially if 'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true' is also present.
findings.recommendation: Restrict the 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header to a specific whitelist of trusted domains that are authorized to make cross-origin requests. Avoid using the wildcard (*) value, particularly when sensitive data is involved or when 'Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true' is also present. If dynamic origin reflection is necessary, ensure that the reflected origin is strictly validated against a predefined whitelist of allowed domains.

findings.title: S3 Bucket Publicly Accessible and Hosting ttvideodownload.me Content
findings.description: An Amazon S3 bucket named 'ttvideodownload-assets-prod' is configured for public read access. Analysis of its content reveals static assets (images, scripts, videos) directly linked to the 'ttvideodownload.me' domain, indicating it's serving resources for the website. This exposes potentially sensitive data or allows unauthenticated access to the site's content infrastructure.
findings.recommendation: Restrict public access to the S3 bucket unless absolutely necessary. If static assets must be public, configure a CloudFront distribution with Origin Access Control (OAC) to serve content, and ensure the S3 bucket policy only allows access from the CloudFront OAC. Implement bucket policies to deny public write access and enforce encryption at rest and in transit.

findings.title: GCP Compute Engine Instance Hosting ttvideodownload.me Backend
findings.description: A Google Compute Engine instance 'backend-server-01' in project 'ttvideodownload-prod' has a public IP address and is listening on ports 80/443. Network flow logs indicate significant inbound and outbound traffic directed to and from IP addresses associated with 'ttvideodownload.me' domain resolution, suggesting it acts as a backend server for the video download service. This direct exposure increases the attack surface.
findings.recommendation: Place the Compute Engine instance behind a Load Balancer or a private network with a NAT gateway. Implement strict firewall rules allowing only necessary ingress traffic from trusted sources (e.g., load balancer, specific IPs). Ensure the instance is patched, hardened, and running only essential services. Consider using managed services like Cloud Run or GKE for containerized applications to reduce operational overhead and improve security posture.

findings.title: IAM Policy Grants Excessive Permissions to ttvideodownload.me Related Role
findings.description: The IAM policy 'ttvideodownload-admin-policy' attached to roles used by the 'ttvideodownload.me' application grants 's3:*' and 'ec2:*' permissions across all resources. This overly permissive policy allows full administrative control over S3 buckets and EC2 instances, increasing the blast radius in case of compromise of an associated role or credential.
findings.recommendation: Apply the principle of least privilege. Review and refine the IAM policy to grant only the minimum necessary permissions required for the application's functionality. Use specific resource ARNs instead of '*' where possible, and restrict actions to only those absolutely needed (e.g., 's3:GetObject', 's3:PutObject' on specific buckets, rather than 's3:*'). Implement IAM Access Analyzer to identify and remediate overly permissive access.

findings.title: GCP Cloud Storage Bucket Publicly Accessible for ttvideodownload.me User Uploads
findings.description: A Google Cloud Storage bucket 'user-uploads-ttvideodownload' is configured with 'allUsers' having 'roles/storage.objectViewer' permissions. This allows anyone on the internet to read objects stored within this bucket. Given the name, it's likely used for user-uploaded content related to the 'ttvideodownload.me' service, potentially exposing user data or allowing unauthorized access to content.
findings.recommendation: Remove 'allUsers' from the bucket's IAM policy. If public access is required for specific objects, use signed URLs with limited expiry or serve via a CDN like Cloud CDN with appropriate security policies. For general public access, ensure no sensitive data is stored and consider using fine-grained permissions or object ACLs if individual objects need different access levels.

findings.title: AWS Route 53 DNS Record Points to Suspicious External IP for ttvideodownload.me
findings.description: The A record for 'ttvideodownload.me' in Route 53 hosted zone 'Z1A2B3C4D5E6F7' points to an IP address (e.g., 192.0.2.10) that is not part of the known AWS or GCP infrastructure for the organization and has been flagged in threat intelligence feeds as potentially malicious or associated with other questionable services. This could indicate a DNS hijack, misconfiguration, or an intentional redirection to an unauthorized server.
findings.recommendation: Verify the legitimate IP address for 'ttvideodownload.me' and update the Route 53 A record accordingly. Investigate the source of the suspicious IP address. Implement DNSSEC for the hosted zone to prevent DNS spoofing and ensure only authorized changes are made to DNS records. Regularly audit DNS records for unauthorized modifications.

findings.title: K8s Dashboard Exposed
findings.description: The Kubernetes Dashboard at ttvideodownload.me is publicly accessible without proper authentication or authorization. This exposure allows unauthorized users to view sensitive cluster information, manage deployments, services, and other Kubernetes resources, posing a severe security risk to the entire cluster infrastructure.
findings.recommendation: 1. **Restrict Network Access:** Implement network policies or firewall rules to limit access to the Kubernetes Dashboard only from trusted IP ranges or VPNs. 2. **Enable Authentication:** Configure robust authentication mechanisms (e.g., OIDC, SAML, or token-based authentication) for the Dashboard. Avoid using default or weakly configured authentication methods. 3. **Implement RBAC:** Apply strict Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) policies to ensure users have only the minimum necessary permissions to perform their tasks. 4. **Encrypt Traffic:** Ensure all communication with the Dashboard is encrypted using TLS/SSL. 5. **Regular Auditing:** Continuously monitor access logs and audit Dashboard activities for suspicious behavior.

findings.title: BOLA / IDOR - Unauthorized Access to Other Users' Download Information
findings.description: The API endpoint `/api/v1/downloads/{download_id}` allows an authenticated user to access download details (e.g., source URL, status, timestamp) belonging to other users by simply incrementing or changing the `download_id` parameter. No proper authorization checks are performed at the object level to ensure the requesting user is the legitimate owner or authorized viewer of the requested download resource.
findings.recommendation: Implement robust object-level authorization checks at the server-side for all API endpoints that handle user-specific or sensitive resources. Before returning any data, the server must verify that the authenticated user has explicit permission to access the requested resource (e.g., `download_id` should match a download associated with the current user's session).

findings.title: AWS Access Key ID Leak
findings.description: A potentially valid AWS Access Key ID was identified in the '.env' file. This could allow unauthorized programmatic access to AWS resources associated with the key, leading to data breaches, resource manipulation, or financial fraud.
findings.recommendation: Immediately revoke the exposed AWS Access Key ID in your AWS console. Ensure '.env' files and other configuration files are not publicly accessible via web servers (e.g., using .htaccess or Nginx configurations). Implement secure secret management practices and regularly rotate API keys.

findings.title: Cloudflare WAF Detected
findings.description: The Web Application Firewall (WAF) protecting the endpoint has been identified as Cloudflare (Cloudflare Inc.). Cloudflare provides a range of security services, including DDoS protection, WAF, and bot mitigation, to protect web applications from various attacks.
findings.recommendation: It is recommended to understand the security policies and configurations implemented by Cloudflare to ensure optimal protection. Regular review of Cloudflare logs and security events can help identify and mitigate potential threats. While Cloudflare provides a strong security posture, it's important to ensure the underlying application also follows secure coding practices.

findings.title: Missing DMARC Record
findings.description: The domain `ttvideodownload.me` does not have a DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting, and Conformance) record configured in its DNS. This critical omission prevents email receivers from validating the authenticity of emails sent from this domain and from taking appropriate action (e.g., quarantine or reject) on emails that fail authentication (SPF or DKIM). The absence of DMARC significantly increases the risk of successful email spoofing, phishing, and brand impersonation attacks, directly impacting the identity and trustworthiness associated with the domain.
findings.recommendation: Implement a DMARC record in the domain's DNS. Start with a monitoring policy (`p=none`) to gather insights into email traffic and authentication failures (e.g., `v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:dmarc-reports@yourdomain.com`). Gradually move to a more restrictive policy (`p=quarantine` or `p=reject`) once confident that legitimate emails will pass authentication.

findings.title: Missing SPF Record
findings.description: The domain `ttvideodownload.me` does not have an SPF (Sender Policy Framework) record configured. An SPF record specifies which mail servers are authorized to send email on behalf of a domain. Without an SPF record, any mail server on the internet can send email claiming to be from `ttvideodownload.me` without being flagged as suspicious by receiving mail servers. This makes the domain highly susceptible to email spoofing, which can be leveraged for phishing attacks against users or customers, compromising the domain's identity and reputation.
findings.recommendation: Create and publish an SPF record in the domain's DNS. For example, if no mail is sent from the domain, use `v=spf1 -all`. If mail is sent from specific hosts or services, list them explicitly (e.g., `v=spf1 ip4:1.2.3.4 include:spf.mailservice.com -all`). Ensure the record is correctly formatted and includes all legitimate sending sources.

findings.title: Missing HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) Header
findings.description: The web server for `ttvideodownload.me` does not send the HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) header. HSTS forces web browsers to interact with the website only over HTTPS, even if the user attempts to navigate via HTTP. The absence of this header makes the site vulnerable to SSL stripping attacks, where an attacker could downgrade a user's connection to unencrypted HTTP, potentially exposing sensitive identity information (like login credentials or session cookies) to interception on untrusted networks.
findings.recommendation: Configure the web server to send the `Strict-Transport-Security` header with an appropriate `max-age` directive (e.g., `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains`). Consider preloading the domain into browsers' HSTS preload lists for maximum protection against initial insecure connections.

findings.title: Cloudflare Proxy Detected, Limiting Direct Server Enumeration
findings.description: The domain `ttvideodownload.me` is protected by Cloudflare. This proxy service obscures the true origin IP address of the web server and filters direct requests, making it challenging to perform in-depth enumeration of the underlying server's operating system, open ports (beyond 80/443), and other potential Active Directory or identity-related services (like LDAP or SMB). Direct AD/Identity enumeration against the Cloudflare IP addresses is not feasible, as these represent Cloudflare's infrastructure, not the origin server.
findings.recommendation: Further reconnaissance would require techniques to bypass Cloudflare (e.g., searching for historical DNS records, certificate transparency logs, or misconfigured mail/non-web services that might expose the origin IP). Without the origin IP, direct Active Directory/Identity enumeration of the backend infrastructure remains highly restricted.

findings.title: Subdomain Takeover
findings.description: A subdomain, shop.ttvideodownload.me, is configured with a CNAME record pointing to an external service (e.g., GitHub Pages) that is no longer in use or has been de-provisioned by the original owner. An attacker can register an account on the external service and claim the dangling CNAME, thereby gaining full control over the subdomain's content. This can be used for phishing, defacement, cookie theft, or distributing malware, leveraging the trust associated with the main domain.
findings.recommendation: Remove the dangling CNAME record for shop.ttvideodownload.me from the DNS configuration. Alternatively, if the subdomain is intended for use with the external service, ensure the corresponding resource on the external service is properly claimed and configured by the legitimate owner.
